metadata.title: Treat Each Digit as a Variable with a Place
metadata.description: Solve missing-digit equations by place value, column carries, and digit constraints.

content.text: In an alphametic, every digit has a place value and every column has a carry. Start with the units column because it often fixes the carry immediately.
For equations such as 5p9+327+2q8=1114, expand by place value and reduce the equation to a relation among p and q. Then maximize or minimize the requested digit under the digit bounds.
Let's solve a same-star addition using carries.
Do not brute-force all ten digits unless the structure fails. Column arithmetic and place-value equations usually reduce the possibilities to one or two cases.
Now reduce a missing-digit equation to p+q.
Finish with a repeated-digit multiplication pattern.
Excellent. Digit puzzles are now column arithmetic with constraints, not guesswork.
